summary: Week three of a three-week-old account: 13 messages, 5 from Kaitlynn, 8 from ALTR. The single biggest thing that happened is what didn't happen. Kaitlynn's one named milestone — the Aug 19 drop of brand-new, never-sold content she flagged on day one ('all content uploaded aug 19th is brand new never sold. go crazy!!') — landed inside this window and was not mentioned by a single person in the chat. The last message in the group is from Aug 18, so the drop date and the two days after it are dead air. Separately, on 2026-08-14 she asked for a call, Mayson said yes and asked for a time, she gave her availability within a minute ('I will be available anytime after 12:30 Eastern time :)'), and no time was ever proposed — 7 days later it is still unbooked. That 8/14 exchange also carried a direct product request ('would love a couple wall post a day - scheduled out an advance is totally fine - as well as story posts') that nobody has acknowledged. Note for continuity: the nine messages sent on 2026-08-14 were not covered by last week's run, so these items are surfacing here for the first time. The genuinely good news is billing finally started — Stephski sent the first invoice on 8/15 covering Aug 7-14 with banking and Zelle details, closing the biggest flag from last week's report — and Michelle delivered a complete IG reels brief with a guide, inspo and Drive link on 8/17 and answered Kaitlynn's clarifying question in four minutes. Kaitlynn remains warm and vocally happy ('I am really impressed and thankful for the numbers and efforts in the account'), which is exactly why the pattern underneath is worth naming: there are now four separate client asks sitting unanswered — the Aug 7 voice-memo offer (14 days), the call (7 days), the posting-cadence request (7 days), and her invoicing question 'is it weekly or bi-weekly typically?' (4 days). No complaints have been made. The risk is that a client this agreeable stops asking rather than starts complaining.
